headline: Nussmeier, LSU ground game wear down Miami in fourth quarter
dek: LSU opens the season 1-0 and atop the Eastern Southern while Miami falls to 0-1 with a road test at Washington looming.
body: With 2:24 left in the fourth quarter, LSU faced second and goal at the Miami 2; Garrett Nussmeier handed to Rico McNeil, who punched in a 2-yard touchdown and Lilian Munoz added the extra point to make it 38-27, the largest lead of the night at 11 points.

Miami struck first when Graham Mertz hit Gunner Benton for a 16-yard touchdown and a successful two-point try put the Hurricanes up 8-0 at 11:45 of the first quarter; Nussmeier answered with a 14-yard keeper and a two-point conversion to knot it at 8. A Vencie Sites field goal and a Romeo Dixon 2-yard run pushed Miami ahead 18-8 before Nussmeier found Paul Barnhardt for a 15-yard score to cut the gap to 18-15. A safety on a Nussmeier sack sent Miami into halftime leading 20-15. LSU opened the third quarter with a 75-yard drive capped by a 20-yard Nussmeier-to-Woody Hasty strike for a 21-20 lead, then a 39-yard Munoz field goal made it 24-20. Mertz hit Colby Lilly for a 14-yard touchdown to reclaim a 27-24 edge, but LSU responded with an 11-play, 73-yard march finished by Tim Ferguson's short touchdown run for a 31-27 advantage early in the fourth. The final LSU drive covered 82 yards in 12 plays, ending with McNeil's go-ahead score.

LSU won the turnover battle decisively, forcing three Miami giveaways — two Mertz fumbles recovered by Thaddeus Chadwick and Elisha Neal, plus a Kolaj Cobbins interception — while committing only one lost fumble themselves. The Tigers controlled the clock at 32:45 to 27:15 and leaned on 181 rushing yards against 103 for Miami, even as the Hurricanes outgained them through the air 318 to 200. Nussmeier was efficient at 15-of-26 for 204 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions, good for a 108.5 rating and 10th in the league in passing yards after Week 1. Mertz threw for 322 yards and two scores but the three turnovers proved costly. Chimere Dike paced all receivers with 103 yards on three catches, while Colby Lilly led Miami on the ground with 79 yards on 10 carries, ranking fifth in the PCFL in rushing yards. LSU's defense, which allowed 421 total yards (11th in the league), bent but forced the critical stops, including a fourth-down incompletion at the Miami 38 with 1:37 remaining.

The win vaults LSU to 1-0, first in the Eastern Southern and No. 1 in the power poll, while Miami drops to 0-1, fourth in the division and No. 10 in the poll. LSU averages 38 points scored and allows 27 per game through one week; Miami mirrors those marks in reverse at 27 scored and 38 allowed. Next up, LSU travels to face Arizona State (0-1), and Miami visits Washington (1-0).
turningPoint: LSU's 12-play, 82-yard touchdown drive culminating in Rico McNeil's 2-yard run at Q4 2:24 extended a 31-27 lead to 38-27 and effectively sealed the game.
byTheNumbers: Turnover margin: LSU forced three Miami takeaways (two fumbles, one interception) while losing only one fumble.
Time of possession: LSU held the ball for 32:45 compared to Miami's 27:15, grinding the Hurricanes' defense with sustained drives in the second half.
Rushing disparity: LSU outrushed Miami 181-103, with Tim Ferguson and Rico McNeil each scoring a fourth-quarter touchdown that flipped the game.
Third-down efficiency: LSU converted 4 of 9 (44%) versus Miami's 3 of 9 (33%), extending drives that wore down the Miami front seven.

unsungHero.name: Rico McNeil
unsungHero.why: Came off the bench to deliver the go-ahead 2-yard touchdown run with 2:24 remaining, capping an 82-yard drive that turned a four-point lead into an 11-point cushion.
